title: Champions League semi-finals set after Bayern Munich, Arsenal progress
content:
The men’s Champions League semi-finals are set, following the conclusion of the quarter-final ties on Wednesday.

In Germany, Bayern Munich and Real Madrid played out perhaps the game of the season, as the home side won 4-3, securing a 6-4 aggregate victory after last week’s 2-1 win in the Spanish capital. The match had four lead changes, a red card and multiple goalkeeper mistakes, while Bayern’s Harry Kane scored his 50th goal of the season.

Elsewhere, Arsenal were held to a goalless draw at home against Sporting CP, with Mikel Arteta’s side progressing after their 1-0 win in Portugal in the first leg. Each side managed only one shot on target during the game at the Emirates Stadium.

Vincent Kompany’s Bayern will face Paris Saint-Germain in their semi-final, with the French side comfortably beating Liverpool 4-0 on aggregate after 2-0 victories at home and then on Merseyside.

Arsenal will come up against Atletico Madrid, who made it through despite losing 2-1 at home to Barcelona on Tuesday. Atletico’s surprise 2-0 win in Barcelona last week proved decisive.

The first leg of the semi-finals will be played on Tuesday, April 28 and Wednesday, April 29, with the second legs a week later on May 5 and May 6. UEFA has not yet released the fixture information for the ties.

The final will take place on Saturday, May 30 — 11 days before the start of the World Cup — at the Puskas Arena in Hungary.

Analysis by Seb Stafford-Bloor, Dermot Corrigan and Anantaajith Raghuraman

Analysis by Art de Roche and Jack Lang
